sources.note: Classified 'Unattested'; alternative names Amala, Mala, Rumaiya, Rumaya, Tumala; no descriptive references at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology; only Temple 1922 and Gunn 1956 ethnographic overviews, Ethnologue, LL-MAP).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93(1): 45-67. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210 (open access, CC-BY).
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any East Kainji language; the phonology section (pp. 56-58) covers consonants, vowels and tones of Boze and Amo only. For Mala it records no data: Table 1 (p. 48) gives Mala status '?' with no source, where '? signifies no information'; p. 47: 'Many languages, especially of the Western branch appear to have no material available at all.' Mala is in that Western branch.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (3rd ed. 2012 PDF on rogerblench.info).
sources.note: Would give the entry-level data note for Mala/Rumaiya (location, sources, whether any wordlist exists); the only remaining overview not opened. Unlikely to contain a stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1314323.
sources.note: Only names 'Mala-Ruma' in the East Kainji tree; Appendix A (Tables 30-31, pp. 102-103) lists no data source for Mala; no Mala forms and nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research. Ms. (version for the Hamburg meeting proceedings), Cambridge, 2 Oct 2004. rogerblench.info (Internet Archive copy 2025-05-28).
sources.note: Earlier draft of the 2020 article. Lists 'Mala-Ruma' in the Kauru cluster (Appendix 1); the 'arm/hand' comparative table (p. 11) has blank rows for Mala and Ruma, i.e. no data. Nothing on stress.
